name: Herrera 2018, eq. (22): Darmois matching condition [P_r]_Sigma = 0

source.located: arXiv:1801.08358v2 [gr-qc], L. Herrera, 'New definition of complexity for self-gravitating fluid distributions: The spherically symmetric, static case' (dated 8 Feb 2018; v2 7 Feb 2018), section II.A, p.3, eqs (19)-(22)
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1801.08358 (full pages 1-10 returned, v2 PDF text); eqs (1)-(13), (19)-(22), (32) and the 'necessary and sufficient' sentence read verbatim at source in this audit

published_statement: p.3: 'For the exterior of the fluid distribution, the spacetime is that of Schwarzschild: [eq (19)]. In order to match smoothly the two metrics above on the boundary surface r = r_Sigma = constant, we require the continuity of the first and the second fundamental forms across that surface, producing e^{nu_Sigma} = 1 - 2M/r_Sigma (20), e^{-lambda_Sigma} = 1 - 2M/r_Sigma (21), [P_r]_Sigma = 0 (22) ... Eqs. (20), (21), and (22) are the necessary and sufficient conditions for a smooth matching of the two metrics (1) and (19) on Sigma.' Since the exterior (19) is vacuum, [P_r]_Sigma = 0 means P_r(r_Sigma^-) = 0.
published_hypotheses: H1 static, spherically symmetric metric (1) in Schwarzschild-like coordinates, ds^2 = e^nu dt^2 - e^lambda dr^2 - r^2 dOmega^2
H2 the metric is SOURCED: Einstein field equations G^nu_mu = 8 pi T^nu_mu (2) hold inside, with T the fluid's own stress tensor (self-gravitating distribution)
H3 locally anisotropic fluid, T = diag(mu, -P_r, -P_perp, -P_perp) in Bondi's local Minkowski frame, comoving observer (eqs 3-5)
H4 the fluid is BOUNDED by a spherical surface Sigma at r = r_Sigma = constant
H5 the EXTERIOR is VACUUM Schwarzschild (19) with mass M
H6 SMOOTH matching: continuity of the first AND second fundamental forms across Sigma (Darmois) -- i.e. no thin shell / surface layer on Sigma
H7 (implicit in eq 20) the exterior time coordinate normalised so that [h] = 0 carries no constant rescaling factor -- a coordinate choice
H8 general relativity (Einstein-Hilbert); no statement is made for other theories
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at the use site -- VACUUM EXTERIOR (H5). tolman.py:2396-2398 turns '[P_r]_Sigma = 0' into 'a BOUNDED source has p_r = 0 at the cut'. [P_r]_Sigma = 0 is a CONTINUITY statement; it yields p_r = 0 only because Herrera's exterior (19) is vacuum. With any stressed exterior (e.g. a charged body: the RN exterior has T^r_r = -Q^2/(8 pi r^4) != 0, or cavity walls beyond the cut) continuity gives p_r(Sigma^-) = the exterior's radial stress, not 0. 'Bounded' carries this only if it is read as 'T = 0 everywhere outside Sigma'; the file does not name it. The canonical hypothesis list (bounded source 'matched smoothly to an exterior') names no exterior.

DROPPED at the use site -- NO SURFACE LAYER (H6). tolman.py:2396-2402 (the L1 label 'GIVEN p_r = 0 at the cut') states boundedness only. Re-derived here (C1-C2, E1, F1): with (20),(21) holding and P_r(r_Sigma) = p0 != 0 the Israel shell has zero surface energy and a tangential stress proportional to p0; on a fixed background the delta-coefficient of div T is -P(R) + nu'(R) sigma/2 - 2s/R. A bounded traceless source WITH a (traceless) shell has p_r(R^-) = p0 != 0 (worked example F). The canonical hypothesis 'matched smoothly' does carry H6, and the file separately REFUSES 'a ball enclosing a mirror' (tolman.py:549, 2494) -- a mirror is a surface layer -- so this is a drop at the L1 site, partly covered elsewhere in the file.

CLASS TRANSFER NOT STATED -- SOURCED vs TEST-FIELD (H2). Herrera's (20)-(22) are derived for a SELF-GRAVITATING fluid: the second fundamental form jumps because the fluid sources the metric. tolman.py's scope is the opposite class: 'TEST-FIELD-background ... NOTHING SOURCED -- THEOREM X shows the exactly-sourced class is empty' (tolman.py:2486-2491; BACKGROUND_HYPOTHESIS tolman.py:2439; HYPOTHESES_ADDED tolman.py:2419; section 2 tolman.py:214). On a fixed smooth background the extrinsic curvature of r = const is trivially continuous, so Herrera's derivation does not apply to L1's class as cited. The CONCLUSION does transfer, by a different route: distributional conservation nabla_mu T^mu_r = 0 on ANY fixed background (re-derived here, D1 reproduces Herrera eq (9); E2) forces p_r(R^-) = 0 given no surface layer and vacuum outside. So the GIVEN is true in the tree's class under H5+H6, but on a ground the tree does not cite; the cited ground is a sourced-geometry theorem the same file says has an empty exact class.

WEAKENED dependency, in the tree's favour -- the matching condition is NOT load-bearing for L1's TOTAL-mass conclusion. For a bounded source, a cut placed anywhere OUTSIDE all matter has p_r = 0 because T = 0 there, with no matching condition at all; the identity m(R) = 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) then gives m = 0 (worked example F3: interior m = 4 pi R^3 p0 is cancelled exactly by the traceless shell's 4 pi R^2 sigma = -4 pi R^3 p0). Eq (22) is load-bearing only if 'the cut' is the source's own boundary approached from inside and 'm' excludes any surface layer. tolman.py:2399-2402 does not say which cut is meant; its PEER_STATUS row (tolman.py:2621-2625) reaches '4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 for ANY ball enclosing the whole device' via von Laue, which is the outside-cut reading.

NO DRIFT on 'necessary AND sufficient' (tolman.py:2514-2517 quotes it). Re-derived (B1-B5): [K^theta_theta] = 0 <=> (21); given (21), [K^t_t] = 0 <=> P_r(r_Sigma) = 0; and (21)+(22) => every mixed K component matches. Necessity holds given H6 (no shell); eq (20) is [h] = 0 up to a constant rescaling of t (H7), a coordinate choice. The tree's quotation is accurate.

NO DRIFT on theory (H8): tolman.py works in GR; later literature (Rosa 2103.11698) shows smooth-matching conditions ADD constraints ([R], [T], [d R], [d T]) in f(R,T) but keep [h] = [K] = 0, so nothing in the tree's GR use is affected.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (22 checks, exit 0; output in rederive/1801.08358-eq22.out). A1-A3: eqs (6), (7) reproduced from the computed Einstein tensor of metric (1), and eq (10) nu' = 2(m + 4 pi P_r r^3)/(r(r-2m)) from (7)+(12). B0-B5: extrinsic curvature of r = const is K^t_t = e^{-lam/2} nu'/2, K^th_th = e^{-lam/2}/r (one common sign); against Schwarzschild, [K^th_th] = 0 <=> eq (21) <=> m(r_S) = M; given (21), [K^t_t] = 0 <=> P_r(r_S) = 0 (eq 22); (21)+(22) suffice. Herrera's 'necessary and sufficient' CONFIRMED. C1-C2: if P_r(r_S) = p0 != 0 with (20),(21), the Israel shell has S^t_t = 0 and S^th_th = -p0 r_S^{3/2}/(2 sqrt(r_S - 2M)) (sign per convention) -- necessity needs 'no thin shell'. D1: nabla_mu T^mu_r = 0 on a FIXED background is Herrera eq (9). E1-E2: distributionally, delta-coefficient -P(R) + nu'(R) sigma/2 - 2s/R; no surface layer => p_r(R^-) = 0 on any fixed background (the test-field route to eq (22)'s conclusion). F0-F4: counterexample to 'bounded => p_r = 0 at the cut' with a surface layer: flat traceless p_r = p_t = p0, u = 3 p0 inside R plus a traceless shell s = -p0 R/2, sigma = -p0 R; p_r(R^-) = p0 != 0, m(R^-) = 4 pi R^3 p0 (identity holds), m(R^+) = 0 (L1's total-mass conclusion survives with the cut outside). G1-G3: in-class positive control p_r = A(R^2 - r^2)^2 gives m(r) = 4 pi r^3 p_r(r) at every r and m(R) = 0.

later_literature.what: States the GR smooth-matching conditions as continuity of the induced metric and the extrinsic curvature ([h_ab] = [K_ab] = 0), a nonzero [K] implying a thin shell -- the frame Herrera's (20)-(22) instantiate. In f(R,T) the smooth set gains [R] = [T] = [d R] = [d T] = 0 (eq 54). Confirms the GR statement; EXTENDS by showing the set is theory-dependent -- irrelevant to the tree, which is GR.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence runs against it here. Eq (22) is a THEOREM of differential geometry plus the Einstein equations -- it has NO numerical inputs (no G, c, masses, or measured constants enter; M and r_Sigma are free symbols), so there is no datum the author could have lacked in 2018 and none that has moved. The re-derivation in this audit reproduces it exactly in both directions (B1-B5). Later work (Rosa 2021, general-theory junction papers 2021-2026) changes the conditions only by changing the THEORY of gravity, which is a hypothesis (H8), not missing data. What the tree's use does lack is two NAMED hypotheses at the site (vacuum exterior; no surface layer) and an explicit statement that the conclusion transfers to its test-field class by conservation rather than by Herrera's sourced route -- these are hypothesis drifts in the tree, not a defect or data gap in Herrera.
grade_evidence: The PUBLISHED result STANDS: eqs (20)-(22) and 'necessary and sufficient' re-derived exactly with sympy (B1-B5; eqs (6), (7), (10), (9) also reproduced, A1-A3, D1), no numerical input exists to move, no later paper contradicts it in GR. The grade NARROWED is for the result AS THE TREE USES IT (tolman.py:2396-2402, L1): (1) the tree's 'a BOUNDED source has p_r = 0 at the cut' drops, at the site, Herrera's VACUUM exterior (H5) -- [P_r]_Sigma = 0 is continuity, and gives 0 only against vacuum -- and the NO-SURFACE-LAYER hypothesis (H6); worked example F shows a bounded traceless source with a traceless shell has p_r(R^-) = p0 != 0; (2) the tree's class is test-field / not sourced (tolman.py:2439, 2486-2491), where Herrera's sourced derivation does not apply as cited -- the conclusion is recovered here instead from distributional conservation on a fixed background (E2), under H5+H6. Not WRONG: no counterexample exists inside H5+H6, and L1's total-mass conclusion survives even without eq (22) when the cut is outside all matter (F3) -- so this narrows the stated ground of the GIVEN, it does not refute L1. Over-representation checked both ways: nothing here is a defect in Herrera, and the tree's quotation of the source (tolman.py:2514-2517) is accurate.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: tolman.py's L1 GIVEN names 'vacuum outside the cut' and 'no surface layer at the cut' (or 'the cut lies outside all matter'), and cites distributional conservation of T on the fixed background (or the Herrera result explicitly as transferred to the test-field class by that route). To WRONG: a smooth (no-shell) bounded conserved static spherical source on a fixed background with vacuum outside and p_r(R^-) != 0 -- E1/E2 show none exists, so this would require an error in the conservation algebra. To OPEN: none -- the source is read and the claim is finite and checked.
